tone_statements.quote: Nas línguas Chapakura, a acentuação dos lexemas é dedutível do peso silábico - o único fator prosódico fonológico nessa família lingüística. Portanto, o acento não é fonológico por ser previsível. ... A atualização fonética da acentuação lexical obedece às seguintes regras: (a) uma sílaba leve é átona e possui um tom baixo. Em outras palavras, carrega um acento de intensidade (“stress”) fraco e um acento de altura (“pitch”) baixo; (b) uma sílaba pesada é tônica e possui um tom alto. ... [p. 149:] (d) em Oro Win, a proeminência acentual do Protochapakura, que integra a intensidade e a altura, é preservada na sua modalidade “frágil”, tanto nos contextos específicos como globalmente
tone_statements.translation: In the Chapakura languages, the accentuation of lexemes is deducible from syllable weight - the only phonological prosodic factor in this language family. Accent is therefore not phonological, being predictable. ... The phonetic realization of lexical accentuation obeys the following rules: (a) a light syllable is unstressed and has a low tone, i.e. it carries weak intensity accent ('stress') and low pitch; (b) a heavy syllable is stressed and has a high tone. ... (d) in Oro Win, the Proto-Chapakura accentual prominence, which combines intensity and pitch, is preserved in its 'fragile' modality, both in the specific contexts and globally
tone_statements.locator: §2.2 'A estrutura prosódica do lexema', p. 23 (rules (a)-(b)); Oro Win-specific: §3.4 pp. 38-40 (phonemes/allophones), ch. 5 tables pp. 147-148 and conclusion (d) p. 149
tone_statements.summary: No lexical tone. Prosody = syllable weight only: every lexeme is (CV) + heavy syllable (CVC, CVː or CVV), the heavy syllable always lexeme-final; accent (both intensity 'stress' and pitch) is predictable from weight and non-contrastive: light syllable unstressed with low pitch, heavy (final) syllable stressed with high pitch, /#(σ)σ#/ -> [(σ̀)ˈσ́]. For Oro Win specifically the measured intensity…

sources.note: States that in the Chapakura languages (Oro Win included and separately measured) syllable weight is the only phonological prosodic factor; lexical accent is predictable (lexeme = optional light CV + obligatory final heavy CVC/CVː/CVV syllable) hence non-phonological, and is realized phonetically as weak stress + LOW pitch ('tom baixo') on the light syllable and strong stress + HIGH pitch ('tom alto') on the heavy final syllable - i.e. pitch is a redundant correlate of weight, no lexical tone. Chapter 5 gives Oro Win acoustic means (light vs heavy syllable: 14.2 vs 13.7 dB, 46.0 vs 46.4 semit…
